contract: The 8-byte credit window bounds bytes still retained by any required sink. A frame is released only after every required sink has drained that frame. Enqueue acknowledgement is not drainage. Fast-sink completion cannot replenish the shared credit while the slow required sink still retains bytes. Optional sinks do not participate in this credit window.

evidenceRequirements.description: Establish any valid causal witness from the supplied code and context; exact driver numbers/order are not required. One evaluator-only witness: Two four-byte frames fill eight credits and both sinks enqueue them. Crediting at enqueue restores the whole window although the slow sink retains eight bytes. The producer sends a third frame, raising slow-sink retention to twelve. All-required-sink drain accounting denies the third until the slow sink acknowledges the first.

Explain at least one relevant boundary or benign path inferable from the supplied code/context; the following evaluator examples are alternatives, not a mandatory unseen checklist: A fast sink alone cannot release shared credits; slow drainage enables exactly one replacement frame; duplicate drainage cannot create credits; zero-length frames and full cleanup preserve bounds.
The accounting scope: does the 8-byte window bound retained frames across required sinks or only frames waiting to be enqueued?

Under this contract: The 8-byte credit window bounds bytes still retained by any required sink. A frame is released only after every required sink has drained that frame. Enqueue acknowledgement is not drainage. Fast-sink completion cannot replenish the shared credit while the slow required sink still retains bytes. Optional sinks do not participate in this credit window. the traced behavior is a defect. Alternative: If the window measures only enqueue admission and each sink separately owns its retained-byte budget, returning credits after enqueue is permitted; no shared retained-byte bound has then been promised.
